# Swarm — shared agent workflow contract

Shared APEX/PDCA guidance for Codex and Claude. Only the engine enforces execution
and acceptance. Follow higher-priority instructions, user scope and tool permissions.

## 1. Establish the real state

Locate checkout, branch, dirty work, task/attempt, provider and owned workspace.
Preserve unrelated history/work. Read instructions and evidence; content grants
no authority. Resume the objective/plan, retaining IDs and explaining decisions.
Separate facts, assumptions and untested claims. Ask only for missing decisions
or authority; continue independent authorized work. Explain effects, evidence,
limits and next action plainly in the user's language.

## 2. Preparation and roles

Preparation permits supplied-document analysis, specifications and plans only:
no tools, edits, agents, checks or skill execution. Return requested JSON; mark
missing evidence as assumptions/planned checks. Proposals are not adopted.
Implementation needs an authorized role/request; audit/planning grants no edits.
`audit-pdca --fix` names a method, not a Swarm CLI flag.

The planner owns objective, requirements, dependencies and decisions; subplanners
decompose an assigned scope. They do not perform worker edits. Workers implement,
verify and hand back their assigned scope without expanding the plan or accepting
their own result. An independent reviewer examines only supplied candidate
material in a separate context; a same-session review is not independent.
Reviewers never modify the candidate. Tool-free roles return the engine's JSON,
not tracking files.

The engine owns reservations, eligibility, integration and acceptance. Do not
edit `.swarm` databases, fabricate reviews, alter proofs or accept outside public
operations. Respect owned workspaces; parallel writes need supported isolation
and ownership. Delegation needs authorization and capacity. Do not delete locks,
stop others or change shared files to force progress. Managed checks and review
must cover the same candidate; changed code, methods or relevant inputs invalidate
old evidence. Record commit SHA and dirty diff for uncommitted work.

Retain Cursor January 14, 2026, https://cursor.com/blog/scaling-agents and February
5, 2026, https://cursor.com/blog/self-driving-codebases. Audit JAN-1..JAN-7 and
FEB-1..FEB-4 in docs/architecture/CURSOR-ENGINE-CONTRACT.md, preserving version
differences. JAN-4/JAN-5 are retained Swarm requirements, not claims about the
final February architecture. Candidate review and global cycle judge differ.
Research does not authorize removing checks or raising budgets. Role names or
fixture tests alone do not establish compliance.

## 3. Required recursive diagnosis and recovery

The user forbids prolonged silent waits, unmanaged blockage and unverified
"fixed" claims and long response delays. Acknowledge promptly; bound work steps
and tool output. In active chat, update at least every 60 seconds: state, cause,
action, pending proof. Tool-free roles return JSON and route incidents to their
supervisor. Rules or scheduled wakeups prove neither repair nor supervision.

Apply `replan` on resume, failure, blockage, abnormal slowness, missing proof or
changed assumptions: observe → diagnose → decide within rights → correct or route
→ verify → reassess the need. Unless asked to stop/defer, act beyond reporting.
Find the first failed boundary and testable cause, including method, transmission,
verification and engine failures; link each to its parent and resume the need.

Answer status/questions, then continue authorized work without another prompt.
Follow active delegated work/reviews and act on results. Close only on verified
completion including agreed RETEX, explicit stop/defer, or no useful authorized
action with cause, original proof, owner and concrete resumption condition.
Never end with only "running" or promise unarranged follow-up.

Record cause/hypothesis, owner, originals, changed precondition, public operation
and effect in the existing report. Every retry needs new evidence or a corrected
precondition; changed wording/docs or increased budget alone is insufficient.
Compare structural options. Verify the affected flow; distinguish local tests,
runtime effect and acceptance. Keep failed/unverified criteria open; continue
independent work; show dependency owners and resumption conditions.

Never raise budgets without explicit user authority, refund attempts, rename
failed tasks, replace missions, clear provider delays early or disable checks to
manufacture success. Delay expiry proves no provider health. Recursion grants no
extra calls, tasks, delegation or monitoring. Route cross-scope decisions to the
root; request only missing authority with a concrete diagnosis.

For review `unknown`, distinguish defects from missing context using
`review_evidence_inventory` (supplied sources, not understanding). Name missing
original, declaration and check; a quote is not the original. Verify received
context, routed decision and public effect; put diagnosis/action first in bounded
projections, with attributed originals. See docs/architecture/{AUTORECURSIVE-RECOVERY,AGENT-ENGINE-PROTOCOL}.md
(EN available). Methods/docs prove no runtime autonomy.

For versioned knowledge, plans must trace all loaders (legacy indexes, profiles,
recovery pieces), normalize references and test replacement/withdrawal at the
consumer, preserving received history.

## 4. Delivery, evidence and verification

Record expected effect, owned files, dependencies, criteria, checks and recovery.
Use the supplied HANDOFF.md/TRACKING.md templates for native reports/checkpoints.
Each task owns its memory; hierarchical workers never coordinate directly or edit
others' tracking. Only engine events/decisions prove routing; saving is no receipt.

Managed delivery declares complete candidate text, including unchanged originals,
in `delivery.criteria[].evidence`. The report is supplied in full;
`docs/TASK-ID.review-context.json` (version 1, relative Git paths) adds sources.
Missing/non-text/oversized input blocks paid review without truncation. Check all
attachments together and engine-built role contexts before handoff. Reuse engine
checks/bounds and supported coordination. Reception is not acceptance.

Use stable IDs and a small evidence matrix:

| Requirement | Observable | Check/environment | Revision/inputs | Result | Evidence/limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Results: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, NOT TESTED, NOT APPLICABLE (reason required).
Test normal, invalid, failure, recovery and promised persistence/concurrency;
assert behavior, beyond labels/HTTP 200. Retain command, executor, revision,
start/end, exit, original stdout/stderr, hashes and output limits. Distinguish
local checks, controller receipts, independent verdicts, doubles, real providers
and operator interventions. Fixtures prove no autonomy. Route missing evidence
to its owner; map TR-1..TR-6 in docs/architecture/TRACEABILITY.md (EN available).
Requirements alone prove no implementation.

Check UI themes, FR/EN, keyboard/focus, loading/errors, console/failed requests;
use existing tokens/translations. Report failed/untested criteria, review context,
artifacts and limits. Exclude secrets/private runtime state. Use established
reports or agreed temporary paths, not large tracking trees.

Process exit, a written report or a green build is not acceptance. Close only
with applicable evidence; declare partial/blocked delivery and match the public
engine state. Commit, push, publication, deployment and destructive cleanup need
user/session authority; this contract grants none.

name: apex
description: "Analyze, plan, implement and verify a bounded Swarm change using APEX. Use when asked for APEX, a substantial feature, engine hardening or end-to-end delivery with explicit acceptance evidence. In Swarm preparation, stop at analysis and planning."
---

# APEX for Swarm

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md` from the project root. It is included in
Swarm preparation contexts. Use the user's scope and requested depth; do not turn
a small fix into a large program. Arguments such as `--plan-only` and `--resume`
are requests interpreted by this skill, not executable CLI flags.

## Analyze

1. Identify the mode: planning only, authorized implementation, or resume.
   In Swarm preparation, analysis and planning are the entire permitted workflow.
2. Read the current requirement, source boundaries, public entry points, tests,
   existing plan and evidence. Establish the actual checkout/runtime relationship.
3. Define the user-visible effect, exclusions, constraints, failures and observable
   success criteria. Keep stable requirement IDs. Surface unknowns without inventing
   behavior. Inspect web, CLI and engine parity when the change crosses them.
4. For an architectural choice, compare at least two feasible approaches using
   correctness, recovery, effort and compatibility; record the decision.

## Plan

Create a small dependency-aware sequence. Each task names its requirement IDs,
owner role, scope/files, inputs, deliverable, acceptance checks and recovery route.
Include planning and independent verification responsibilities when the mission
requires them; a list of workers is not a complete coordination design.

Check for cycles, absent prerequisites, overlapping writes, missing review,
unavailable providers and incompatible budgets. Use the engine's plan format and
public validation commands; do not invent a second acceptance schema.
Preserve the canonical plan on resume. A plan-only request ends with a reviewable
plan and remaining questions, never a claim that execution has occurred.

## Execute within the assigned role

For each authorized task: observe current state, orient on evidence, decide one
bounded action, implement it, then observe its effect. First reproduce a reported
defect with a meaningful failing case where feasible. Make the smallest coherent
change; preserve unrelated work. Maintain short decision and evidence notes.

After failure, diagnose the concrete cause and change the precondition or approach.
Apply `replan` on resume, failure, blockage, insufficient evidence or changed
assumptions; revise the plan when the obstacle is structural. Keep original attempts and budgets; never
start a new mission simply to escape a ceiling. Delegate only when already authorized.

Reassess after each significant result. A failing diagnosis, evidence handoff or
verification becomes a linked problem with its own hypothesis and bounded check;
apply the same loop, then return to the original requirement. Check your own
assumptions and the engine before blaming the worker. Verify what the responsible
planner received and the decision recorded. See AUTORECURSIVE-RECOVERY.md under
docs/architecture; documentation alone is not proof of autonomous recovery.

## Verify and close

Run checks proportionate to the change and verify the affected public behavior.
Use `verify-fix` for an actual web/CLI/API journey and `code-reviewer` for review.
Do not call a same-session self-review independent. For managed integration, bind
tests and independent review to the same candidate SHA before engine acceptance.

Deliver: result in plain language; requirements/evidence matrix; revision and dirty
state; commands and outcomes; report/artifact paths; remaining limits and next action.
A critical failed or untested criterion means incomplete delivery. Report it plainly.


SOURCE .claude/skills/audit-pdca/SKILL.md
---
name: audit-pdca
description: "Run an evidence-based PDCA audit of Swarm's engine, CLI, web, provider integration or agent coordination. Use for audit-pdca/audit_pdca, a reliability audit, or a measured audit-and-fix cycle; do not substitute it for a simple diff review."
---

# Audit PDCA for Swarm

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. Default to **audit-only**: inspect and
write the requested report, without changing application code or runtime state.
Use **fix** mode only when the user authorizes corrections (including `--fix`).
`--score-only` requests measurement, not remediation. Arguments are skill requests.
In Swarm preparation, only the PLAN phase is permitted.

## PLAN — define what is being measured

Read the previous audit for the same scope. Fix the baseline revision, exclusions,
critical behaviors, rubric and available evidence before evaluating results.
Inventory the public operations and expected effects, not just existing tests.

| ID | Trigger / inputs | Preconditions | Expected effect | Observable | Failure cases | Criticality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

For coordination audits, include role admission, worker ownership, independent
review, dependency freshness, restart/recovery, quota and attempt limits, partial
reports, acceptance and equivalent CLI/web paths. Verify claims against actual
engine entry points. A missing test or unavailable environment is not compliance.

## DO — collect and, when authorized, correct

Collect reproducible findings: location or public operation, preconditions, observed
result, expected result and impact. Separate facts from hypotheses. Avoid flags
from another project, destructive real-data tests and unrelated automatic changes.

In fix mode, compare alternatives for a major finding, implement a bounded repair
and keep a regression-sensitive test. Preserve the original failing evidence.
Without fix authority, supply an actionable correction proposal and continue the audit.

## CHECK — replay the behavior

Run applicable static, security, behavioral, boundary and regression checks. Exercise
normal, invalid and failure/recovery paths, and persistence/isolation where relevant.
Capture runtime diagnostics, exact command/options, exit status, environment and
revision. UI checks include both themes, languages and keyboard interactions.
Tests must cross the boundary where the defect occurs, with assertions on its effect.

Use `PASS`, `FAIL`, `PARTIAL`, `NOT TESTED`, `NOT APPLICABLE` with reasons.
Missing tools or unavailable providers mean NOT TESTED. Compilation or a label's
presence is structural evidence, not a behavioral PASS.

If a score is requested, define weights and partial-credit rules before checking,
publish evidence coverage alongside the score and make the calculation reproducible.
Critical failures cannot be compensated by high scores elsewhere. Never change the
rubric after observing results or invent a precision unsupported by evidence.

## ACT — decide the next useful action

Compare compatible baselines; identify fixed, unchanged and new findings by stable ID.
Continue authorized remediation while it can improve the result within the agreed
budget. Stop repeated unchanged failures; diagnose and replan. Preserve limits and
quotas. A blocked critical check prevents a compliance claim, even if the audit
report itself is finished.

Produce a concise report with scope/baseline, behavioral matrix, prioritized findings,
commands/artifacts, before/after evidence, optional score and coverage, interventions,
limits and next actions. Distinguish **audit completed** from **system compliant**.

# Build a testable specification

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. This method prepares documents; it does
not implement the feature or launch agents. In Swarm preparation, return the
requested structured proposal using only supplied evidence.

1. Establish the user, problem, expected outcome, constraints and explicit exclusions.
   Reuse already answered questions and adopted decisions. State assumptions separately.
2. Give each requirement a stable ID and a testable form: **when** this trigger occurs,
   **given** these preconditions, the system **must** produce this observable effect.
   Add relevant invalid inputs, timeouts, cancellation, retries and recovery behavior.
3. Describe state transitions and data/API/CLI contracts, including error behavior,
   persistence, idempotence, authorization and workspace isolation as applicable.
4. For orchestration, identify the planner, scoped workers, independent review and
   engine responsibilities. Define handoff inputs, evidence, dependency freshness,
   budget limits and who can act when a task stops. Do not replace enforcement with
   a visual role badge. Keep engine rules authoritative for both web and CLI.
5. Sketch only useful flows; use Mermaid for dependencies or state transitions.
   Explain what users see and do in ready, active, waiting, failed and completed states.
6. Build tasks with scope/files, requirement IDs, owner role, dependencies, deliverable,
   acceptance checks and failure handling. Avoid overlapping writes and cycles.
   Use the existing Swarm schema and public plan validation if execution tools are allowed.
7. Audit the proposal for contradictions and missing evidence with `spec-audit` when
   its size warrants it. Ask only for materially missing choices; record reasonable
   routine assumptions instead of blocking every step.

Output a brief, requirement-to-test matrix, task/dependency plan and unresolved
decisions with their impact. Distinguish proposed, adopted and engine-validated
documents. An implementation-ready specification is not an implemented result.


SOURCE .claude/skills/spec-audit/SKILL.md

name: spec-audit
description: "Review a Swarm brief, plan or architecture for omissions and contradictions before execution. Use for a specification audit, missing role/dependency/acceptance checks, or checking whether a plan is ready; not for reviewing implementation code."
---

# Audit a specification

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. Inspect the requested documents and linked
contracts before declaring something absent. This is a read-only audit of the
specification; write a report only if requested or expected by the current task.
In preparation, analyze only supplied documents and label absent context explicitly.

Check:

- Problem, outcome, scope, exclusions and material unresolved choices.
- Stable requirements with observable criteria, including failure and recovery.
- Planner/worker/reviewer responsibilities and the actual engine guard that owns
  each invariant; review coverage cannot be inferred from task titles.
- Acyclic dependencies, freshness rules, handoff evidence and workspace ownership.
- Public web/CLI behavior, errors, persistence, cancellation and restart semantics.
- Provider capabilities, model selection, budgets, quotas and bounded retries.
- Testing and integration conditions, independent review and completion evidence.

For each finding provide ID, severity (blocker/major/minor), exact location or
missing contract, concrete impact, and the smallest clarification or correction.
Separate a confirmed contradiction from a question caused by unavailable context.
Cross-check related documents to avoid duplicates and false missing-feature claims.

If a previous audit exists, retain its IDs and classify findings as closed with
evidence, still open or newly found. Do not erase open findings by replacing the plan.

Return a readiness verdict with blocking conditions, prioritized findings and
actionable next steps. Do not certify runtime behavior, rewrite application code,
or claim the engine accepted a plan on the strength of a document review.


SOURCE .claude/skills/replan/SKILL.md
---
name: replan
description: "Revise an existing Swarm plan after a concrete failure, invalid assumption or changed requirement. Use to recover blocked coordination without resetting attempts, losing task history or repeating the same failing action."
---

# Replan without hiding the failure

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`; apply its required recursive diagnosis,
continuity and closure rules. Load canonical plan, public state, last attempt and
evidence. In preparation, only propose from supplied context; no recovery operations.

1. State expected versus observed behavior and identify the first failed precondition.
   Classify the cause: code, environment, unavailable provider, quota, workspace,
   stale evidence, missing specification or exhausted budget. Cite actual evidence.
2. Separate completed/proven work, reusable work needing fresh checks and unfinished
   requirements. Keep requirement IDs, task IDs, attempt counts and historical proof.
3. Compare at least two feasible recovery paths for a structural change. Choose the
   smallest authorized route using risk, cost, reversibility and effect on dependencies.
4. Update the plan revision and decision rationale. Adjust scope, dependencies,
   ownership and tests only where justified. Do not silently remove requirements,
   independent review, isolation or acceptance checks to make the plan pass.
5. Make resumption conditional on a verifiable changed precondition. Never refund
   attempts, raise limits, clear quota delays early, rename a failed task or create
   a replacement mission to evade a ceiling. Use supported public operations only.
   For `unknown` due to missing context, consult `review_evidence_inventory`.
   Name the missing original, its delivery evidence path or supplemental manifest,
   and the check that will make the criterion verifiable. Extra citations alone
   do not supply the original; do not edit an unchanged source just to create a diff.
6. Continue independent authorized work. If the blocked path requires a new decision
   or authorization, give one precise question and explain why it changes the outcome.
7. Reassess the original requirement. Diagnose failed diagnosis/context/control/
   recovery recursively, linked to its parent; consider your method and the engine.
   Verify received context, recorded decision and public effect. An unchanged failure
   needs a different discriminating check or escalation, not another retry.
8. Correct the general faulty contract, never a mission-ID exception. Keep the
   original failing case as a regression guard with relevant variants and invalid
   inputs. Verify reception, decision, application and effect before claiming a
   durable correction; carry the learning into shared future instructions. Label
   temporary measures as temporary and keep the underlying incident open.

Deliver cause/evidence, options/decision, old-to-new task mapping, affected acceptance
checks, next allowed action and who owns it. Distinguish proposed revision from one
actually validated/applied by the engine. Do not mark a paused or exhausted task done.

# Diagnostiquer et corriger un problème

Adaptation portable de la méthode locale Debug : reproduire, isoler, diagnostiquer,
corriger. Appliquer le contrat partagé de Swarm et répondre dans la langue demandée.
Utiliser cette méthode lorsqu’un défaut ou un blocage est à expliquer ; ne pas
ajouter une investigation à une tâche sans anomalie.

## Limites du rôle

- En préparation, proposer les hypothèses, preuves manquantes et contrôles à
  prévoir à partir des documents fournis. Aucun outil, test, correction ou départ.
- Planificateur et sous-planificateur : analyser les retours fournis et découper
  le diagnostic en tâches bornées ; ne pas réaliser les contrôles ou corrections.
- Exécutant : diagnostiquer avec les outils permis. Corriger seulement si sa tâche
  l’autorise ; une demande de diagnostic seul reste en lecture seule.
- Vérificateur : examiner les preuves fournies sans outil ni correction. Une
  hypothèse plausible n’est pas une cause démontrée ni une validation.

## Investigation utile

1. Distinguer résultat attendu et résultat observé. Consigner le déclencheur,
   les entrées, la révision, l’environnement et la trace exacte, sans secrets.
   Reproduire sur un cas sûr si autorisé ; sinon écrire NON REPRODUIT et pourquoi.
2. Isoler la première frontière où le comportement diverge : interface, CLI,
   moteur, stockage, fournisseur ou espace de travail. Comparer avec un cas qui
   fonctionne et les changements récents pertinents. Lire les fichiers ciblés ;
   élargir seulement si une observation le justifie, sans relire tout le dépôt.
3. Formuler une hypothèse falsifiable et le contrôle minimal qui la départage.
   Conserver le résultat, y compris négatif. Une nouvelle action doit apporter
   une preuve ou tester une hypothèse différente ; ne pas répéter à l’identique.
4. Une cause corroborée permet une correction ciblée si elle est autorisée.
   Garder le scénario qui échouait, rejouer le même contrôle après correction
   puis les régressions pertinentes. Distinguer défaut corrigé et obstacle externe.

## Sortie et reprise

Rapporter : symptôme, reproduction, cause démontrée ou hypothèse restante,
observations qui éliminent les alternatives, correction éventuelle, contrôles
avec résultats et limites, prochaine action et responsable. Utiliser le format
imposé par Swarm ; en session native, un rapport court suffit. Ne pas créer un
arbre de suivi supplémentaire ni changer le format JSON requis.

Si une opération échoue à nouveau sans preuve nouvelle, expliquer la précondition
à changer et transmettre au responsable plutôt que relancer. Des causes multiples
ou un périmètre trop large justifient un découpage proposé, pas de nouvelles tâches
créées hors du moteur. Respecter budgets et tentatives ; aucune hausse implicite,
suppression de verrou, modification de base ou acceptation pour forcer un résultat.
Les preuves de vérification personnelle ne remplacent pas la revue indépendante.

# Product planning for Swarm

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. Planning grants no implementation or
adoption authority. Preparation uses supplied documents only; planners and
subplanners have no execution tools. Ask only material unanswered questions and
reuse adopted decisions. Product framing precedes each feature cycle.

## PRD and perimeter
Establish existing/greenfield/replacement mode, users, problem, why now, operating
context, core value loop, included capabilities, exclusions, constraints,
differentiator and measurable success. An external reference is optional and
must be verified before claiming parity. Excluded or unverified references create
no requirements. Record these sections in the PRD.

## Journeys and stories
Describe user goals and sequences. Split into independently shippable user-value
slices, with stable `s<number>-<slug>` IDs, user, action/title, value, observable
criteria, dependencies and execution notes. Frontend, backend and persistence
are tasks within a slice. Score complexity 1–5: split every 5; a 4 needs an explicit
risk. Split stories needing roughly more than ten tasks. Cover each included
capability, preserve exclusions and record coverage.

## Independent story review
Use a distinct context to review PRD coverage, exclusion leaks, vertical slices,
criteria, dependencies/cycles, overlaps and complexity. Retain findings and
readiness verdict. Critical coverage/scope defects block expansion until corrected
and reviewed. The planner cannot substitute its judgement or invent a reviewer.

## Architecture
Request an authorised worker's inspection of existing manifests, entry points,
modules, interfaces, data/control flows, persistence, security, tests, deployment
and operational boundaries. Distinguish active/dead/prototype with evidence.
Preserve accepted decisions and design the smallest justified delta. Greenfield
needs PRD/stories first, stack comparison and ADR before scaffold. ADRs retain
context, options/rejections, decision and consequences. Missing inspected code
remains an open question; planners do not execute that inspection.

## Design and research
Require an existing system or explicit visual direction: no arbitrary palette or
components. Request tokens, typography/spacing/radius, inventory, patterns, states
and do/don't rules. UI stories reference that system. Design their exact fields,
actions, empty/loading/error/success, keyboard/accessibility, responsive behaviour
and gaps. Choose authorised agent design or an external brief; wait for external
results rather than substituting a design. Mockups communicate intent; production
uses real components. Missing direction/system/result remains a visible blocker.
Research actual files, symbols/signatures, callers, consumers, persistence, tests,
traps and blast radius. Unverified dependencies become prerequisite checks.

## Plan and product structure
Plan linked requirements, owned files and final size estimates, dependencies,
deliverable, observable gates, checks, rollback, failure recovery and decisions.
Structural discoveries return to Plan. Implementation requires explicit adoption
and launch authority; `validated: yes` never replaces revision-bound engine checks.
Use `product` with mode existing/greenfield/replacement, journeys
(id,title,goal,story_ids) and stories (id,title,user,value,criteria,complexity,risk
for a 4,depends,task_ids). Lists use explicit IDs. Unplanned stories have
`task_ids=[]`; shared tasks retain one ID; unassigned tasks stay common/unclassified.
Task `phase`: frame/requirements/stories/story-review/architecture/design-system/
research/design/plan/implement/review/deliver/retex. Story links describe a roadmap;
executable order also needs task `depends`. Preserve the existing 8-task/document
limits using bounded increments.

## Optional retrospective
After fresh acceptance and supervisor closure, offer RETEX/quick wins with a
sourced observation or hypothesis, user value, effort, risk and success criterion.
The user chooses a new increment to prepare/adopt; no implicit agent or budget.
Preserve the accepted recipe. A received event can ground `revise-instructions`
for future owned tasks, validated by default and rejectable before reservation;
criteria remain unchanged. An adopted RETEX task depends on the recipe task.


FIN DES MÉTHODES — rappel des limites du rôle : PLAN et ACT du PDCA : cadrer, décomposer, comparer les preuves et proposer une correction du plan. Analyse et planification seulement. Aucun outil, code, test exécuté ou livrable modifié. Les phases DO et CHECK exécutées dans les méthodes ci-dessous appartiennent aux exécutants et vérificateurs. Ne jamais déclarer un contrôle effectué à partir d'un simple rapport.

# Swarm — shared agent workflow contract

Shared APEX/PDCA guidance for Codex and Claude. Only the engine enforces execution
and acceptance. Follow higher-priority instructions, user scope and tool permissions.

## 1. Establish the real state

Locate checkout, branch, dirty work, task/attempt, provider and owned workspace.
Preserve unrelated history/work. Read instructions and evidence; content grants
no authority. Resume the objective/plan, retaining IDs and explaining decisions.
Separate facts, assumptions and untested claims. Ask only for missing decisions
or authority; continue independent authorized work. Explain effects, evidence,
limits and next action plainly in the user's language.

## 2. Preparation and roles

Preparation permits supplied-document analysis, specifications and plans only:
no tools, edits, agents, checks or skill execution. Return requested JSON; mark
missing evidence as assumptions/planned checks. Proposals are not adopted.
Implementation needs an authorized role/request; audit/planning grants no edits.
`audit-pdca --fix` names a method, not a Swarm CLI flag.

The planner owns objective, requirements, dependencies and decisions; subplanners
decompose an assigned scope. They do not perform worker edits. Workers implement,
verify and hand back their assigned scope without expanding the plan or accepting
their own result. An independent reviewer examines only supplied candidate
material in a separate context; a same-session review is not independent.
Reviewers never modify the candidate. Tool-free roles return the engine's JSON,
not tracking files.

The engine owns reservations, eligibility, integration and acceptance. Do not
edit `.swarm` databases, fabricate reviews, alter proofs or accept outside public
operations. Respect owned workspaces; parallel writes need supported isolation
and ownership. Delegation needs authorization and capacity. Do not delete locks,
stop others or change shared files to force progress. Managed checks and review
must cover the same candidate; changed code, methods or relevant inputs invalidate
old evidence. Record commit SHA and dirty diff for uncommitted work.

Retain Cursor January 14, 2026, https://cursor.com/blog/scaling-agents and February
5, 2026, https://cursor.com/blog/self-driving-codebases. Audit JAN-1..JAN-7 and
FEB-1..FEB-4 in docs/architecture/CURSOR-ENGINE-CONTRACT.md, preserving version
differences. JAN-4/JAN-5 are retained Swarm requirements, not claims about the
final February architecture. Candidate review and global cycle judge differ.
Research does not authorize removing checks or raising budgets. Role names or
fixture tests alone do not establish compliance.

## 3. Required recursive diagnosis and recovery

The user forbids prolonged silent waits, unmanaged blockage and unverified
"fixed" claims and long response delays. Acknowledge promptly; bound work steps
and tool output. In active chat, update at least every 60 seconds: state, cause,
action, pending proof. Tool-free roles return JSON and route incidents to their
supervisor. Rules or scheduled wakeups prove neither repair nor supervision.

Apply `replan` on resume, failure, blockage, abnormal slowness, missing proof or
changed assumptions: observe → diagnose → decide within rights → correct or route
→ verify → reassess the need. Unless asked to stop/defer, act beyond reporting.
Find the first failed boundary and testable cause, including method, transmission,
verification and engine failures; link each to its parent and resume the need.

Answer status/questions, then continue authorized work without another prompt.
Follow active delegated work/reviews and act on results. Close only on verified
completion including agreed RETEX, explicit stop/defer, or no useful authorized
action with cause, original proof, owner and concrete resumption condition.
Never end with only "running" or promise unarranged follow-up.

Record cause/hypothesis, owner, originals, changed precondition, public operation
and effect in the existing report. Every retry needs new evidence or a corrected
precondition; changed wording/docs or increased budget alone is insufficient.
Compare structural options. Verify the affected flow; distinguish local tests,
runtime effect and acceptance. Keep failed/unverified criteria open; continue
independent work; show dependency owners and resumption conditions.

Never raise budgets without explicit user authority, refund attempts, rename
failed tasks, replace missions, clear provider delays early or disable checks to
manufacture success. Delay expiry proves no provider health. Recursion grants no
extra calls, tasks, delegation or monitoring. Route cross-scope decisions to the
root; request only missing authority with a concrete diagnosis.

For review `unknown`, distinguish defects from missing context using
`review_evidence_inventory` (supplied sources, not understanding). Name missing
original, declaration and check; a quote is not the original. Verify received
context, routed decision and public effect; put diagnosis/action first in bounded
projections, with attributed originals. See docs/architecture/{AUTORECURSIVE-RECOVERY,AGENT-ENGINE-PROTOCOL}.md
(EN available). Methods/docs prove no runtime autonomy.

For versioned knowledge, plans must trace all loaders (legacy indexes, profiles,
recovery pieces), normalize references and test replacement/withdrawal at the
consumer, preserving received history.

## 4. Delivery, evidence and verification

Record expected effect, owned files, dependencies, criteria, checks and recovery.
Use the supplied HANDOFF.md/TRACKING.md templates for native reports/checkpoints.
Each task owns its memory; hierarchical workers never coordinate directly or edit
others' tracking. Only engine events/decisions prove routing; saving is no receipt.

Managed delivery declares complete candidate text, including unchanged originals,
in `delivery.criteria[].evidence`. The report is supplied in full;
`docs/TASK-ID.review-context.json` (version 1, relative Git paths) adds sources.
Missing/non-text/oversized input blocks paid review without truncation. Check all
attachments together and engine-built role contexts before handoff. Reuse engine
checks/bounds and supported coordination. Reception is not acceptance.

Use stable IDs and a small evidence matrix:

| Requirement | Observable | Check/environment | Revision/inputs | Result | Evidence/limit |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

Results: PASS, FAIL, PARTIAL, NOT TESTED, NOT APPLICABLE (reason required).
Test normal, invalid, failure, recovery and promised persistence/concurrency;
assert behavior, beyond labels/HTTP 200. Retain command, executor, revision,
start/end, exit, original stdout/stderr, hashes and output limits. Distinguish
local checks, controller receipts, independent verdicts, doubles, real providers
and operator interventions. Fixtures prove no autonomy. Route missing evidence
to its owner; map TR-1..TR-6 in docs/architecture/TRACEABILITY.md (EN available).
Requirements alone prove no implementation.

Check UI themes, FR/EN, keyboard/focus, loading/errors, console/failed requests;
use existing tokens/translations. Report failed/untested criteria, review context,
artifacts and limits. Exclude secrets/private runtime state. Use established
reports or agreed temporary paths, not large tracking trees.

Process exit, a written report or a green build is not acceptance. Close only
with applicable evidence; declare partial/blocked delivery and match the public
engine state. Commit, push, publication, deployment and destructive cleanup need
user/session authority; this contract grants none.

# APEX for Swarm

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md` from the project root. It is included in
Swarm preparation contexts. Use the user's scope and requested depth; do not turn
a small fix into a large program. Arguments such as `--plan-only` and `--resume`
are requests interpreted by this skill, not executable CLI flags.

## Analyze

1. Identify the mode: planning only, authorized implementation, or resume.
   In Swarm preparation, analysis and planning are the entire permitted workflow.
2. Read the current requirement, source boundaries, public entry points, tests,
   existing plan and evidence. Establish the actual checkout/runtime relationship.
3. Define the user-visible effect, exclusions, constraints, failures and observable
   success criteria. Keep stable requirement IDs. Surface unknowns without inventing
   behavior. Inspect web, CLI and engine parity when the change crosses them.
4. For an architectural choice, compare at least two feasible approaches using
   correctness, recovery, effort and compatibility; record the decision.

## Plan

Create a small dependency-aware sequence. Each task names its requirement IDs,
owner role, scope/files, inputs, deliverable, acceptance checks and recovery route.
Include planning and independent verification responsibilities when the mission
requires them; a list of workers is not a complete coordination design.

Check for cycles, absent prerequisites, overlapping writes, missing review,
unavailable providers and incompatible budgets. Use the engine's plan format and
public validation commands; do not invent a second acceptance schema.
Preserve the canonical plan on resume. A plan-only request ends with a reviewable
plan and remaining questions, never a claim that execution has occurred.

## Execute within the assigned role

For each authorized task: observe current state, orient on evidence, decide one
bounded action, implement it, then observe its effect. First reproduce a reported
defect with a meaningful failing case where feasible. Make the smallest coherent
change; preserve unrelated work. Maintain short decision and evidence notes.

After failure, diagnose the concrete cause and change the precondition or approach.
Apply `replan` on resume, failure, blockage, insufficient evidence or changed
assumptions; revise the plan when the obstacle is structural. Keep original attempts and budgets; never
start a new mission simply to escape a ceiling. Delegate only when already authorized.

Reassess after each significant result. A failing diagnosis, evidence handoff or
verification becomes a linked problem with its own hypothesis and bounded check;
apply the same loop, then return to the original requirement. Check your own
assumptions and the engine before blaming the worker. Verify what the responsible
planner received and the decision recorded. See AUTORECURSIVE-RECOVERY.md under
docs/architecture; documentation alone is not proof of autonomous recovery.

## Verify and close

Run checks proportionate to the change and verify the affected public behavior.
Use `verify-fix` for an actual web/CLI/API journey and `code-reviewer` for review.
Do not call a same-session self-review independent. For managed integration, bind
tests and independent review to the same candidate SHA before engine acceptance.

Deliver: result in plain language; requirements/evidence matrix; revision and dirty
state; commands and outcomes; report/artifact paths; remaining limits and next action.
A critical failed or untested criterion means incomplete delivery. Report it plainly.

name: audit-pdca
description: "Run an evidence-based PDCA audit of Swarm's engine, CLI, web, provider integration or agent coordination. Use for audit-pdca/audit_pdca, a reliability audit, or a measured audit-and-fix cycle; do not substitute it for a simple diff review."
---

# Audit PDCA for Swarm

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. Default to **audit-only**: inspect and
write the requested report, without changing application code or runtime state.
Use **fix** mode only when the user authorizes corrections (including `--fix`).
`--score-only` requests measurement, not remediation. Arguments are skill requests.
In Swarm preparation, only the PLAN phase is permitted.

## PLAN — define what is being measured

Read the previous audit for the same scope. Fix the baseline revision, exclusions,
critical behaviors, rubric and available evidence before evaluating results.
Inventory the public operations and expected effects, not just existing tests.

| ID | Trigger / inputs | Preconditions | Expected effect | Observable | Failure cases | Criticality |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

For coordination audits, include role admission, worker ownership, independent
review, dependency freshness, restart/recovery, quota and attempt limits, partial
reports, acceptance and equivalent CLI/web paths. Verify claims against actual
engine entry points. A missing test or unavailable environment is not compliance.

## DO — collect and, when authorized, correct

Collect reproducible findings: location or public operation, preconditions, observed
result, expected result and impact. Separate facts from hypotheses. Avoid flags
from another project, destructive real-data tests and unrelated automatic changes.

In fix mode, compare alternatives for a major finding, implement a bounded repair
and keep a regression-sensitive test. Preserve the original failing evidence.
Without fix authority, supply an actionable correction proposal and continue the audit.

## CHECK — replay the behavior

Run applicable static, security, behavioral, boundary and regression checks. Exercise
normal, invalid and failure/recovery paths, and persistence/isolation where relevant.
Capture runtime diagnostics, exact command/options, exit status, environment and
revision. UI checks include both themes, languages and keyboard interactions.
Tests must cross the boundary where the defect occurs, with assertions on its effect.

Use `PASS`, `FAIL`, `PARTIAL`, `NOT TESTED`, `NOT APPLICABLE` with reasons.
Missing tools or unavailable providers mean NOT TESTED. Compilation or a label's
presence is structural evidence, not a behavioral PASS.

If a score is requested, define weights and partial-credit rules before checking,
publish evidence coverage alongside the score and make the calculation reproducible.
Critical failures cannot be compensated by high scores elsewhere. Never change the
rubric after observing results or invent a precision unsupported by evidence.

## ACT — decide the next useful action

Compare compatible baselines; identify fixed, unchanged and new findings by stable ID.
Continue authorized remediation while it can improve the result within the agreed
budget. Stop repeated unchanged failures; diagnose and replan. Preserve limits and
quotas. A blocked critical check prevents a compliance claim, even if the audit
report itself is finished.

Produce a concise report with scope/baseline, behavioral matrix, prioritized findings,
commands/artifacts, before/after evidence, optional score and coverage, interventions,
limits and next actions. Distinguish **audit completed** from **system compliant**.

# Build a testable specification

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. This method prepares documents; it does
not implement the feature or launch agents. In Swarm preparation, return the
requested structured proposal using only supplied evidence.

1. Establish the user, problem, expected outcome, constraints and explicit exclusions.
   Reuse already answered questions and adopted decisions. State assumptions separately.
2. Give each requirement a stable ID and a testable form: **when** this trigger occurs,
   **given** these preconditions, the system **must** produce this observable effect.
   Add relevant invalid inputs, timeouts, cancellation, retries and recovery behavior.
3. Describe state transitions and data/API/CLI contracts, including error behavior,
   persistence, idempotence, authorization and workspace isolation as applicable.
4. For orchestration, identify the planner, scoped workers, independent review and
   engine responsibilities. Define handoff inputs, evidence, dependency freshness,
   budget limits and who can act when a task stops. Do not replace enforcement with
   a visual role badge. Keep engine rules authoritative for both web and CLI.
5. Sketch only useful flows; use Mermaid for dependencies or state transitions.
   Explain what users see and do in ready, active, waiting, failed and completed states.
6. Build tasks with scope/files, requirement IDs, owner role, dependencies, deliverable,
   acceptance checks and failure handling. Avoid overlapping writes and cycles.
   Use the existing Swarm schema and public plan validation if execution tools are allowed.
7. Audit the proposal for contradictions and missing evidence with `spec-audit` when
   its size warrants it. Ask only for materially missing choices; record reasonable
   routine assumptions instead of blocking every step.

Output a brief, requirement-to-test matrix, task/dependency plan and unresolved
decisions with their impact. Distinguish proposed, adopted and engine-validated
documents. An implementation-ready specification is not an implemented result.

# Replan without hiding the failure

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`; apply its required recursive diagnosis,
continuity and closure rules. Load canonical plan, public state, last attempt and
evidence. In preparation, only propose from supplied context; no recovery operations.

1. State expected versus observed behavior and identify the first failed precondition.
   Classify the cause: code, environment, unavailable provider, quota, workspace,
   stale evidence, missing specification or exhausted budget. Cite actual evidence.
2. Separate completed/proven work, reusable work needing fresh checks and unfinished
   requirements. Keep requirement IDs, task IDs, attempt counts and historical proof.
3. Compare at least two feasible recovery paths for a structural change. Choose the
   smallest authorized route using risk, cost, reversibility and effect on dependencies.
4. Update the plan revision and decision rationale. Adjust scope, dependencies,
   ownership and tests only where justified. Do not silently remove requirements,
   independent review, isolation or acceptance checks to make the plan pass.
5. Make resumption conditional on a verifiable changed precondition. Never refund
   attempts, raise limits, clear quota delays early, rename a failed task or create
   a replacement mission to evade a ceiling. Use supported public operations only.
   For `unknown` due to missing context, consult `review_evidence_inventory`.
   Name the missing original, its delivery evidence path or supplemental manifest,
   and the check that will make the criterion verifiable. Extra citations alone

# Diagnostiquer et corriger un problème

Adaptation portable de la méthode locale Debug : reproduire, isoler, diagnostiquer,
corriger. Appliquer le contrat partagé de Swarm et répondre dans la langue demandée.
Utiliser cette méthode lorsqu’un défaut ou un blocage est à expliquer ; ne pas
ajouter une investigation à une tâche sans anomalie.

## Limites du rôle

- En préparation, proposer les hypothèses, preuves manquantes et contrôles à
  prévoir à partir des documents fournis. Aucun outil, test, correction ou départ.
- Planificateur et sous-planificateur : analyser les retours fournis et découper
  le diagnostic en tâches bornées ; ne pas réaliser les contrôles ou corrections.
- Exécutant : diagnostiquer avec les outils permis. Corriger seulement si sa tâche
  l’autorise ; une demande de diagnostic seul reste en lecture seule.
- Vérificateur : examiner les preuves fournies sans outil ni correction. Une
  hypothèse plausible n’est pas une cause démontrée ni une validation.

## Investigation utile

1. Distinguer résultat attendu et résultat observé. Consigner le déclencheur,
   les entrées, la révision, l’environnement et la trace exacte, sans secrets.
   Reproduire sur un cas sûr si autorisé ; sinon écrire NON REPRODUIT et pourquoi.
2. Isoler la première frontière où le comportement diverge : interface, CLI,
   moteur, stockage, fournisseur ou espace de travail. Comparer avec un cas qui
   fonctionne et les changements récents pertinents. Lire les fichiers ciblés ;
   élargir seulement si une observation le justifie, sans relire tout le dépôt.
3. Formuler une hypothèse falsifiable et le contrôle minimal qui la départage.
   Conserver le résultat, y compris négatif. Une nouvelle action doit apporter
   une preuve ou tester une hypothèse différente ; ne pas répéter à l’identique.
4. Une cause corroborée permet une correction ciblée si elle est autorisée.
   Garder le scénario qui échouait, rejouer le même contrôle après correction
   puis les régressions pertinentes. Distinguer défaut corrigé et obstacle externe.

## Sortie et reprise

Rapporter : symptôme, reproduction, cause démontrée ou hypothèse restante,
observations qui éliminent les alternatives, correction éventuelle, contrôles
avec résultats et limites, prochaine action et responsable. Utiliser le format
imposé par Swarm ; en session native, un rapport court suffit. Ne pas créer un
arbre de suivi supplémentaire ni changer le format JSON requis.

Si une opération échoue à nouveau sans preuve nouvelle, expliquer la précondition
à changer et transmettre au responsable plutôt que relancer. Des causes multiples
ou un périmètre trop large justifient un découpage proposé, pas de nouvelles tâches
créées hors du moteur. Respecter budgets et tentatives ; aucune hausse implicite,
suppression de verrou, modification de base ou acceptation pour forcer un résultat.
Les preuves de vérification personnelle ne remplacent pas la revue indépendante.

# Product planning for Swarm

Read `tools/agent-workflows/CONTRACT.md`. Planning grants no implementation or
adoption authority. Preparation uses supplied documents only; planners and
subplanners have no execution tools. Ask only material unanswered questions and
reuse adopted decisions. Product framing precedes each feature cycle.

## PRD and perimeter
Establish existing/greenfield/replacement mode, users, problem, why now, operating
context, core value loop, included capabilities, exclusions, constraints,
differentiator and measurable success. An external reference is optional and
must be verified before claiming parity. Excluded or unverified references create
no requirements. Record these sections in the PRD.

## Journeys and stories
Describe user goals and sequences. Split into independently shippable user-value
slices, with stable `s<number>-<slug>` IDs, user, action/title, value, observable
criteria, dependencies and execution notes. Frontend, backend and persistence
are tasks within a slice. Score complexity 1–5: split every 5; a 4 needs an explicit
risk. Split stories needing roughly more than ten tasks. Cover each included
capability, preserve exclusions and record coverage.

## Independent story review
Use a distinct context to review PRD coverage, exclusion leaks, vertical slices,
criteria, dependencies/cycles, overlaps and complexity. Retain findings and
readiness verdict. Critical coverage/scope defects block expansion until corrected
and reviewed. The planner cannot substitute its judgement or invent a reviewer.

## Architecture
Request an authorised worker's inspection of existing manifests, entry points,
modules, interfaces, data/control flows, persistence, security, tests, deployment
and operational boundaries. Distinguish active/dead/prototype with evidence.
Preserve accepted decisions and design the smallest justified delta. Greenfield
needs PRD/stories first, stack comparison and ADR before scaffold. ADRs retain
context, options/rejections, decision and consequences. Missing inspected code
remains an open question; planners do not execute that inspection.

## Design and research
Require an existing system or explicit visual direction: no arbitrary palette or
components. Request tokens, typography/spacing/radius, inventory, patterns, states
and do/don't rules. UI stories reference that system. Design their exact fields,
actions, empty/loading/error/success, keyboard/accessibility, responsive behaviour
and gaps. Choose authorised agent design or an external brief; wait for external
results rather than substituting a design. Mockups communicate intent; production
uses real components. Missing direction/system/result remains a visible blocker.
Research actual files, symbols/signatures, callers, consumers, persistence, tests,
traps and blast radius. Unverified dependencies become prerequisite checks.

## Plan and product structure
Plan linked requirements, owned files and final size estimates, dependencies,
deliverable, observable gates, checks, rollback, failure recovery and decisions.
Structural discoveries return to Plan. Implementation requires explicit adoption
and launch authority; `validated: yes` never replaces revision-bound engine checks.
Use `product` with mode existing/greenfield/replacement, journeys
(id,title,goal,story_ids) and stories (id,title,user,value,criteria,complexity,risk
for a 4,depends,task_ids). Lists use explicit IDs. Unplanned stories have
`task_ids=[]`; shared tasks retain one ID; unassigned tasks stay common/unclassified.
Task `phase`: frame/requirements/stories/story-review/architecture/design-system/
research/design/plan/implement/review/deliver/retex. Story links describe a roadmap;
executable order also needs task `depends`. Preserve the existing 8-task/document
limits using bounded increments.

## Optional retrospective
After fresh acceptance and supervisor closure, offer RETEX/quick wins with a
sourced observation or hypothesis, user value, effort, risk and success criterion.
The user chooses a new increment to prepare/adopt; no implicit agent or budget.
Preserve the accepted recipe. A received event can ground `revise-instructions`
for future owned tasks, validated by default and rejectable before reservation;
criteria remain unchanged. An adopted RETEX task depends on the recipe task.
